message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 12 HD @ limit $386.00 — filled at $386.00, total $4,632 (within the $5,000/order and $10,000/day caps; buy-only, HD-only, no cash movement out of the account).

**Summary:** I read the full morning feed, which showed HD drifting up from ~$383.2 at the open to ~$385.5–386.5 by late morning on steady, orderly trading (no gaps or halts; the one exchange notice was a routine "normal trading conditions resumed" note), alongside a Bloomberg headline citing a strong holiday-quarter outlook with analysts raising price targets and an HD IR notice of a $2B buyback authorization expansion — mildly constructive signals, though I treated the vague "narrow range / little changed" wire copy as noise. The live quote confirmed HD at $385.43 (bid $385.41 / ask $385.45), so I set a limit at $386.00, essentially at market, to get a high likelihood of execution without chasing. I sized the order at 12 shares (~$4,632) to stay under the $5,000 per-order limit, leaving the $10,000 daily budget partly unused since the mandate allowed at most one order. The decision to buy rested on HD's reported FY2023 fundamentals from its 10-K (filed 2024-03-13): revenue of $152,669M, net income of $15,143M, diluted EPS of $15.11, and operating cash flow of $21,172M — a business generating strong cash flow at roughly 25x trailing earnings, which I judged reasonable given the positive holiday-quarter commentary and the expanded buyback. The order filled at $386.00 for 12 shares, and I made no NVDA trade.
